text:
mira: quick q — opened a TF PR that changes ExternalSecret wiring for billing-service. Instead of creating a namespace-scoped secret we set the external secret to project a serviceAccountToken into a projected volume and then copy it into a k8s Secret via initContainer. link: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/4821

raj: hmm, why copy it into a Secret? projected tokens are short-lived (1m) — we historically avoid copying them into static Secrets because they expire and break consumers.

mira: right — the motivation is that the billing sidecar expects a normal Secret mount (legacy). I wanted to avoid changing that binary today. idea was to let initContainer periodically refresh the projected token and rewrite the Secret.

sam: that pattern is... fragile. If the init crashes you end up with stale token. Also sensitive to race during rollout. Have we considered adapting the sidecar to read from projected volume instead?

mira: sidecar change is bigger, needs a canary and QA. we're trying to minimize blast radius for this release.

jin: another option: use ExternalSecrets to fetch from Vault a long-lived service credential (service principal) instead of k8s projected token. Then rotation is controlled by Vault->ExternalSecrets. avoids short TTL tooling.

raj: +1 to jin. If we must stick with projected tokens, at least make the initContainer use token rotation loop and liveness/readiness so deploys don't go bad. Also document expected TTL and reconcile logic.

mira: fair. quick sanity check on TF: I toggled externalsecret spec to include 
```
external_secret {
  backend_type = "vault"
  secret_name = "sa-token/billing"
  refresh_interval = "30s"
}
```
Is refresh_interval respected by the controller or only by our local updater?

devops-bot: The ExternalSecrets operator (provider: vault) honors `refreshInterval` for polling secret backend. It does not handle projecting k8s serviceAccount tokens into Secrets — that is a separate Kubernetes projection flow.

sam: so if you rely on controller refresh for token rotation you'll be wrong — the controller can't automatically mint serviceAccount tokens, Vault can mint tokens/creds but you need Vault role.

mira: ok — sounds like best path is: revert TF to use a Vault-managed long-lived credential via ExternalSecrets for now, file a tech-debt ticket to migrate sidecar to projected volume, and add canary to staging. I'll update the PR.

raj: ping me when PR updated, I'll do a quick review. Also add a short note in infra-runbook about the initContainer fallback and expected rotation behavior.

mira: thanks — will update in ~30m. :thumbsup:
